2027-06-12.title: Saturday of the Tenth Week in Ordinary Time
readings: So we are ambassadors for Christ … be reconciled to God
The Lord is kind and merciful
Let your word be ‘Yes, Yes’ or ‘No, No’
2027-06-12.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 10 (Year I). On a Saturday in Ordinary Time without an obligatory memorial, the optional memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary may be kept. Liturgical colour: green (white for the Saturday memorial of Our Lady).
2027-06-12.verse: So if anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation: everything old has passed away; see, everything has become new!
theo: Today's reading is the heart of the Second Letter to the Corinthians, and one of the deepest pages Paul ever wrote. Why does he work so hard, suffer so much, put up with misunderstanding? “For the love of Christ urges us on, because we are convinced that one has died for all; therefore all have died. And he died for all, so that those who live might live no longer for themselves, but for him who died and was raised for them.” The love of Christ is not only the love we have for him; it is first his love for us, which presses on us and drives us forward. Because of it Paul looks at everyone differently: “From now on, therefore, we regard no one from a human point of view.” Not by caste, wealth, education or usefulness, but as someone for whom Christ died. Then the great announcement: “So if anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation: everything old has passed away; see, everything has become new!” Baptism is not a coat of paint on an old house; it is a new creation. And all of this comes from God, “who reconciled us to himself through Christ, and has given us the ministry of reconciliation.” God was not waiting for us to make the first move: “in Christ God was reconciling the world to himself, not counting their trespasses against them.” Paul sees himself as an ambassador, carrying a message from the King: “we entreat you on behalf of Christ, be reconciled to God.” The reading ends with a mysterious and wonderful exchange: “For our sake he made him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.” The sinless One took our place so that we could take his. The Psalm answers with pure gratitude: “as far as the east is from the west, so far he removes our transgressions from us.”

In the Gospel Jesus continues his teaching on the Law. The Law forbade false oaths and commanded that vows made to the Lord be kept. Jesus goes further: “But I say to you, Do not swear at all,” neither by heaven, nor by earth, nor by Jerusalem, nor by your own head. People swore by these things to make their words sound more solid, and to leave themselves a way out. Jesus wants disciples whose every word can be trusted: “Let your word be ‘Yes, Yes’ or ‘No, No’; anything more than this comes from the evil one.” (The Church has always understood that this does not forbid a solemn oath for a grave reason, such as in a court of law; Jesus is condemning the habit of swearing, and the lies that make it necessary.) Paul's ambassador and Jesus' plain-spoken disciple belong together: the one who carries the message of reconciliation must be someone whose word is true. On this Saturday many parishes keep the memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary. Her whole life is the perfect Yes: “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.” And Saturday evening is the time when many Catholics go to confession before Sunday. The sacrament of Reconciliation is exactly Paul's ministry: a priest, an ambassador for Christ, saying in his name, I absolve you, and the old passing away, and everything becoming new.
outline: Ask: when did you last feel completely new, as if you had been given a fresh start?
Point 1 · The love of Christ urges us on
One died for all, so that we may live no longer for ourselves.
God reconciles the world in Christ and makes us his ambassadors.
The disciple's word is simple and true, like Mary's Yes.
“If anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation.”
live: If you have not been to confession recently, go this weekend; if you have, pray for someone who is afraid to go.
For one whole day, avoid exaggerations and the phrase I swear; let your yes be yes and your no be no.
2027-06-12.prayer: Father of mercy, in Christ you reconciled the world to yourself, not counting our trespasses against us. You made him who knew no sin to be sin for our sake, so that in him we might become your righteousness. We thank you for the new creation that began in our Baptism, and for every time you have made us new in the sacrament of Reconciliation. Let the love of Christ urge us on, so that we live no longer for ourselves. Make our words simple and true, and teach us to say Yes to you as Mary did. Amen.
altar: At every Mass, over the chalice, the priest repeats the words of Jesus: this is the chalice of my Blood, poured out for you and for many for the forgiveness of sins. Here is the source of the ministry of reconciliation Paul speaks of: the one who died for all is present on the altar, and his sacrifice is offered so that we who live may live for him. Before Communion we confess, Lord, I am not worthy, and he answers by giving himself.

quick: The love of Christ urges us on: one died for all, so that those who live may live no longer for themselves but for him.
If anyone is in Christ there is a new creation; God reconciled the world to himself in Christ and has made us ambassadors of reconciliation.
Jesus asks his disciples not to swear at all but to let their word be Yes, Yes or No, No; Mary's Yes is the model.
2027-06-12.action: Go to confession this weekend, or help someone else to go.
2027-06-12.question: Do people trust my word without my needing to swear or exaggerate?

family.explain: St Paul says that when we belong to Jesus, we become a new creation: the old is gone, the new has come! God wants to make friends with everyone again, through Jesus. That is what happens in confession: God forgives us and makes us new. Jesus also teaches us to always tell the truth, so that our yes means yes and our no means no.
family.intention: We pray for priests who hear confessions, and for people who are afraid to come back to God.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there something we need to say sorry for in our family? Who will be the first to make peace?”

illus: A woman in Alappuzha had not been to confession for almost thirty years. Every Saturday evening she walked past the church on her way to the market and saw the short line near the confessional. One Saturday in the rain she stepped inside only to wait for the shower to pass. The priest was sitting there with no one in front of him. She told him later that she sat down intending to say only good evening, Father, and then everything came out. When she left, the rain had stopped and the road was shining. She said to her daughter: I felt like a new person. Her daughter, who knew 2 Corinthians 5:17 from school, said: Amma, you are a new creation. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord Jesus, your love urges us on. Make us new creatures, ambassadors of your reconciliation, and people whose word can be trusted. Amen.
share: The love of Christ urges us on (2 Corinthians 5:14). Does the love of Christ move me, or do I move only when others push me?
So if anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation (2 Corinthians 5:17). What old thing in my life does Christ want to pass away?
Let your word be Yes, Yes or No, No (Matthew 5:37). Where do I bend the truth, exaggerate or make promises I do not keep?
pm.resp: The Lord is kind and merciful.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a faithful ambassador of the reconciliation God offers in Christ.
For priests who hear confessions, that they may be patient, merciful and wise.
For those who have been away from the sacraments for many years, that they may come home and find a welcome.
For nations, communities and families torn apart, that they may be reconciled.
For our group, through the prayers of the Virgin Mary, that our yes may be like hers.
pm.close: Merciful Father, as far as the east is from the west, so far you remove our sins from us. Make us new in Christ, and send us out as his ambassadors. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, why did St Paul work so hard? Why did he travel, suffer, write letters with tears? He tells us today: for the love of Christ urges us on (2 Corinthians 5:14). Christ died for all, so that those who live might live no longer for themselves, but for him who died and was raised for them (2 Corinthians 5:15). When you really know that someone has died for you, you cannot go on living only for yourself.

Then Paul says one of the most hopeful sentences in the Bible: if anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation: everything old has passed away; see, everything has become new! (2 Corinthians 5:17). God does not just repair us. He makes us new. That happened at our Baptism, and it happens again every time we come back to him in the sacrament of Reconciliation.

And notice who makes the first move. Not us. In Christ God was reconciling the world to himself, not counting their trespasses against them (2 Corinthians 5:19). God came looking for us. And he has given this message to the Church, so that Paul can say: we are ambassadors for Christ; be reconciled to God. Every priest in the confessional is such an ambassador. If you have been away from confession for a long time, this weekend is a good time to come home.

In the Gospel Jesus asks for honesty: let your word be Yes, Yes or No, No (Matthew 5:37). We do not need to swear by God or by our mother's head. A Christian's simple word should be enough. Today is Saturday, a day the Church often gives to Our Lady. Her Yes to God was simple and complete: let it be with me according to your word. May she help us to say Yes to God's reconciliation, and to be people whose word is true. Amen.
kids: Children, have you ever broken something and wished you could have a brand-new one? St Paul says that when we belong to Jesus, God makes us new inside: the old is gone, the new has come! When we say sorry to God in confession, he makes our hearts new and clean again. Jesus also says: always tell the truth. When you say yes, mean yes; when you say no, mean no. Mother Mary said a big Yes to God. Let us say Yes to him too!

intro: The love of Christ that urges us on, the new creation and the ministry of reconciliation, and the simple Yes of the disciple.

points.h: The love of Christ urges us on
sub: Seeing no one from a human point of view.
q: I led them with cords of human kindness, with bands of love.
And he died for all, so that those who live might live no longer for themselves, but for him who died and was raised for them.
points.apply: This week, do one thing each day that you would not do for yourself, simply for the love of Christ.

q: as far as the east is from the west, so far he removes our transgressions from us.
So we are ambassadors for Christ, since God is making his appeal through us; we entreat you on behalf of Christ, be reconciled to God.
points.apply: Make a good confession this week, and invite one person to come with you.

sub: A word that can be trusted.
q: Those who walk blamelessly, and do what is right, and speak the truth from their heart;
Let your word be ‘Yes, Yes’ or ‘No, No’; anything more than this comes from the evil one.
points.apply: For this week, give up the habit of swearing or exaggerating, and keep every small promise you make.

concl: Christ died for all so that we might live for him; in him we are a new creation, reconciled to God and sent as his ambassadors.
Jesus asks for a simple and truthful word; Mary's Yes shows us how to answer God.
2027-06-12.resolve: This week, be reconciled to God in confession, and let your yes be yes and your no be no.
